newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers want competition on Fed services.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers want competition on Fed services.

text.p: Democratic lawmakers introduced a bill on Thursday to help private companies compete with the Federal Reserve in providing basic banking services like check processing and electronic funds tranfers.

Rep. Henry Gonzalez of Texas and Rep. Carolyn Maloney of New York said the Fed was subsidizing banks by offering such services at cut rate prices. Their bill would force the Fed to match its costs and revenues in the provision of 15 specific services.
"Private companies should be allowed to compete on a fair basis with the Fed's thriving business enterprises," Gonzalez said at a news briefing here.
Gonzalez, ranking minority member of the House Banking Committee, said the Fed expects to take in about $810 million this year from various financial service operations.

In 1980, Congress passed the Monetary Control Act which required the Fed to balance costs and revenues to prevent it from undercutting private sector competition. But the Fed has measured costs and revenues from all services in one combined accounting.
Rep Maloney said this comprehensive accounting allowed the to offer some services "well below cost."
